newsitem.title: USA: Hearing on Indianapolis arena brings out support.
newsitem.headline: Hearing on Indianapolis arena brings out support.

text.p: A hearing Tuesday night on a new arena for the Indiana Pacers basketball team elicited a show of support for the plan, city and team officials said Wednesday.

Gail Brown, manager of business communications for Indianapolis Mayor Stephen Goldsmith, said most of the 150 to 200 people that attended the hearing before the city-county council's Municipal Corporations Committee voiced support for a new arena.
Brown said future hearings may be put on hold until the city pulls together a financing plan for the arena, estimated to cost $150 million to $175 million.

She said the financing plan was contingent on action by the Indiana Legislature to provide some funding mechanisms for the plan. Two options currently being considered by lawmakers are proposals to hike the car rental tax in the Indianapolis area and to install slot machines at an area race track, Brown said.
Arena funding was removed from a third option that would add a surcharge onto the admittance fee to gambling boats in the state, she added.
In addition, the city is looking for some infrastructure funding from the state, Brown said.
David Kahn, vice president and assistant general manager for the Pacers, said the team was also willing to help pay for the arena, but has not cited an amount of its contribution.
"We are waiting for the city to come up with a financing plan," he said. "We are willing to participate."

In the meantime, the team has agreed to pay $1.4 million for preliminary architechtural and construction work, he said, adding that the Pacers hope to break ground on the arena by June 1 so the building is ready for the 1999 season.
Kahn added that the team, which occupies the fifth smallest market in the National Basketball Association, is not threatening to leave if it doesn't get a new arena.
"We have to have building revenues to survive," he said, pointing out the team's current home, Market Square Arena, lacks both suites and club seats.
Kahn said Tuesday's hearing provided the team with "a wonderful night" given the support for the arena.
